decisions.reason: A newly launched handle family with several models represents tooling and design investment that management will not write off after one year, and early modest visibility can be attributed to the normal ramp-up in the planning and specification cycle.
The mitred handle family required dedicated engineering and finishing investment, and any slow uptake in its first year is readily explained by long architectural specification lead times.
Although it is a single model with less invested and little public commitment, its multifunctional design fits the firm's announced barrier-free direction, so management will give it more time.
As a multi-model handle line already in the coordinated range, dropping it so soon would expose the launch decision as premature while results can still be blamed on market ramp-up.
The collection has its own page, was publicly showcased as new, and won the German Design Award, making it a visible flagship commitment that the firm will defend.
A finish option costs little to maintain, applies across coordinated product families, and fits the firm's emphasis on in-house finishing, so there is no pressure to remove it.
